newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa bonds soft, rand recovers against mark.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa bonds soft, rand recovers against mark.

text.p: 1405 GMT - South African long bonds continue lower in range in quiet late dealings. Rand maintaining strength versus dollar, recovers against German mark.

* Key R150 long bond last yielding 14.965 from Friday's 14.915 close having made brief afternoon lunge at key psychological level of 15.00 pct. New ceiling emerging around 14.97-98. Dealers say Telkom forward sales might ignite demand in money market.
* Rand last at 4.4605/4635 on dollar from 4.4620/4650 late Friday. Dealers say unit supported by dollar slide. Currency recovers against mark, continues to weaken against yen.
Dealers saw some positive impact on money market rates stemming from the $1 billion sold forward as part of the part privatisation of Telkom

"People are being reminded by the Telkom privatisation that there is a hell of a lot of dollars coming to the market in what is quite a thin one at the moment, so that could jolt it (higher) quite significantly," one said.

South Africa is due to close a deal for the sale of 30 percent of state-run Telkom to a U.S.-Malaysian consortium at 1500 GMT on Wednesday in Cape Town, after which there will be an exchange of cash for shares.

Some $260 million of the amount will go to the exchequer to retire state debt and will not impact the market. But $1 billion will be deposited in Telkom's private sector bank account to help fund infrastructure growth.

"The Reserve Bank will then simply pay the rand into the acount of Telkom at the predetermined rate. Obviously it will have an impact on the money market but the Reserve Bank, through its normal market activities, will smooth the position," Koen Kruger, head of asset management at the Ministry of Finance said earlier.
Bond Exchange data showed foreigners still hungry for local debt having scooped up 257.53 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after selling 25.79 million rand's worth on Thursday.
The purchases took total foreign buys for the year to date to nearly 12 billion rand.
On the money market major banks kept their three month NCD rates steady at 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent.

The Reserve Bank of South Africa reported the money market shortage held steady at 7.826 billion rand on Saturday from 7.783 billion rand on Friday. Friday's total was down from 8.955 billion rand on Thursday.
